evidence.excerpt: The attenuation provided by Y-capacitors in common-mode EMC filters depends on the impedance of the protective earth (PE) connection, which varies substantially between industrial installations. This paper characterises PE impedance at 47 industrial sites across northern Serbia using a vector network analyser, finding that impedance magnitude at 1 MHz ranges from 0.4 Ω to 18 Ω and exhibits significant inductive character above 500 kHz. The measured impedance profiles are used as input to a circuit simulation of a 15 kW drive with a three-stage CM filter, evaluating worst-case degradation in CM insertion loss. CM attenuation at 1 MHz degraded by up to 9 dB between the best and worst PE cases, rendering a filter that passed IEC 61800-3 Category C2 under laboratory conditions non-compliant in 14% of simulated field conditions. A modified filter topology using a split CM choke with partial differential-mode rejection reduces this variability to within ±2 dB.
